sources.articleTitle: Congress government paying ₹80,000 crore per year for debts left behind by KCR: Revanth

headline: Chief Minister Revanth Reddy Criticizes Previous Administration Debt
seoTitle: Chief Minister Criticizes Previous Government Debt
metaDescription: Chief Minister Revanth Reddy reports significant annual debt payments inherited from the previous administration while pledging local water access.
aiSummaryBullets: Chief Minister Revanth Reddy stated the current government pays 80,000 crore rupees annually toward debts incurred by the former leadership.
The administration intends to provide Krishna River water to the Kodangal region by the end of December.
Project goals include providing irrigation support to local lands currently experiencing water scarcity.
aiContextParagraph: The current administration in Telangana, led by Chief Minister Revanth Reddy, has publicly addressed the fiscal challenges resulting from previous government policies. According to the Chief Minister, the state is currently allocating 80,000 crore rupees every year to service debts left by the former administration under K. Chandrashekar Rao. Alongside these financial disclosures, the government has announced infrastructure initiatives aimed at agricultural development. Specifically, the Chief Minister pledged to supply water from the Krishna River to the Kodangal area by December 2026. This project is intended to irrigate parched agricultural lands in the region, which has reportedly suffered from water shortages. The comments highlight an ongoing political discourse regarding the state's fiscal health and development priorities as the current government manages inherited economic burdens while attempting to fulfill electoral infrastructure promises for its constituents.
whyItIsViral: The story has gained traction due to high public interest in regional government fiscal transparency and infrastructure promises as the new year approaches.
